issues.body: json_ld_equal_inner makes arrays unordered whenever in_list is false. The recursion only sets in_list for a key named @list, so the value of {"@value": ..., "@type":"@json"} is compared with unordered-array semantics. For example, an @json payload [1,2] is considered equal to [2,1]. JSON arrays inside an @json literal retain ordinary JSON ordering, so a real compaction bug that reorders them would not fail json_literal_round_trips despite the module explicitly claiming to pin @json payload shape. This makes the central round-trip oracle unsound for one of its advertised invariants.
issues.fix_hint: Make the comparator context-aware for @json value objects: when an object has @type == @json, compare its @value subtree using exact JSON semantics (object member order insignificant, array order significant recursively). Add a witness assertion/test proving that @json payloads [1,2] and [2,1] are unequal, ideally alongside the existing round-trip case.
issues.title: Equality oracle ignores significant array order inside @json literals

verdict.summary: The added coverage exercises the shipping expand/compact paths across many useful JSON-LD shapes, but its equality oracle is not sound for @json values. It treats every array outside an @list as unordered, including arrays nested inside an @json literal, although those arrays are ordinary JSON and their order is significant. Consequently the advertised losslessness test can pass after a compaction regression that reorders JSON payload arrays, contradicting the test's stated invariant and leaving a load-bearing case vacuously accepted.
